family.tagline: A design agency, a rover in progress and one Companion Core.
family.story: Ruth runs a small design agency from the library lounge, and Noam writes robotics software at a standing desk upstairs. At weekends he builds a rover for the garden. One Companion Core on the credenza serves them both.

companion.name: Dahlia
companion.job: Drafts replies to Ruth’s clients from the short notes she sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Ruth reads and sends every message.

companion.name: Lupin
companion.job: Fills in supplier order forms in its own browser from Noam’s parts lists.
companion.limits: Fills in the form only. Noam checks it and places the order.

popup.title: The parcel crosses the kitchen
popup.body: A parcel waits at the front door. Noam carries the Companion Core through the kitchen to its credenza in the lounge.

popup.title: Ruth empties the parcel
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Ruth lays them out beside the credenza.

popup.title: One press wakes the Core
popup.body: Noam plugs in the cable and Ruth presses the button. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Ruth joins on her phone
popup.body: On her phone, Ruth opens the Wi-Fi settings and joins the Core’s own network. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: Ruth picks Hermes, Noam OpenClaw
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Ruth picks Hermes and Noam picks OpenClaw. They add Nextcloud and Gitea, then walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Dahlia says hello
popup.body: Ruth messages the agent she named Dahlia. Dahlia answers from the Core across the room.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: ruth
say.text: Hello, Ruth. I am Dahlia. What is first on the list?

beats.capability: stream your own music collection to any device

popup.title: The old CDs play again
popup.body: Sun reaches the rug while Ruth plays albums she ripped from old CDs. Navidrome streams them from the Core to her phone over the home Wi-Fi.

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains at the DNS level

popup.title: A slow page loses its banners
popup.body: A slow weather page is all banners, so Noam points the router’s DNS at Pi-hole. It blocks known ad and tracker domains for devices that use it for DNS.

beats.capability: manage customers, sales pipelines, campaigns and support cases in a CRM you host

popup.title: Ruth turns down one enquiry
popup.body: Monday morning, two enquiries arrive and only one fits the month. Ruth quotes one and declines the other. EspoCRM keeps both records on the Core for next time.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: The bakery’s label files arrive
popup.body: Before lunch a bakery’s label files arrive, and Ruth files them in Nextcloud. The originals sit on the Core, not in a rented drive.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core

popup.title: A shortcut for Ruth’s briefs
popup.body: Ruth copies each new client’s details into a folder by hand, so Noam builds her an n8n workflow. When a brief arrives, it opens the Nextcloud folder on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Dahlia drafts the delay note
popup.body: The print shop runs a day late. Ruth messages Dahlia the new date. Dahlia drafts the bakery note on the Core’s local model, and Ruth reads and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: ruth
say.text: Here is the bakery note. Please read it before you send it.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host, working with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Ruth lets the vault choose
popup.body: A client portal wants a new password, so Ruth has VaultWarden make one. It is saved in the household’s vault on the Core and works with the Bitwarden apps.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: Two files become one print file
popup.body: The print shop wants one file, not two. At the trestle table, Ruth merges the artwork and its spec sheet in Stirling-PDF, on the Core itself.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: The olive oil runs low
popup.body: Chickpeas simmer on the range and the oil runs low. Noam adds a bottle to the shopping list in Yuvomi, and Ruth sees it on her phone.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: The oven warranty turns up
popup.body: Thursday afternoon, Ruth feeds a month of receipts through Paperless-ngx on the Core. Every page is read and tagged, so the oven warranty is one search away.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals

popup.title: Ruth makes room for a visitor
popup.body: Noam’s sister visits on Saturday. Ruth adds the visit to the household calendar in Yuvomi. She moves a proof check to Friday, and Noam sees both there.

beats.capability: write and run notebooks, code and data in a browser, on your Core

popup.title: Why does the rover drift left?
popup.body: The rover drifts left on gravel, so Noam plots its wheel data in JupyterLab. Then he asks a model on the Core why, through Open WebUI.

beats.capability: host private Git repositories, pull requests and issues on your Core

popup.title: The steering fix goes to Gitea
popup.body: At the standing desk, Noam pushes a steering fix for his rover to Gitea. The repository sits on the Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: an agent with its own browser and coding tools, running in its own sandbox

popup.title: Lupin fills in the parts order
popup.body: Noam hands his agent Lupin a list of motor parts. Lupin fills in the supplier’s order form in its own browser. Noam reads it and places the order himself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: The logo moves to the deck
popup.body: Afternoon light reaches the deck table, so Ruth takes her laptop out. She reworks a logo in Penpot, saved to the Core in the lounge.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: The orange daisies get a note
popup.body: The orange daisies on the front lawn are still in flower. Ruth adds a photo and a note in HortusFox, so next year she knows how long they last.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos

popup.title: Noam photographs the rover’s wiring
popup.body: Noam props the rover on the lawn and photographs its wiring. His phone backs the photos up to Immich over the home Wi-Fi, into the household’s library.

popup.title: Two gables, one Core
popup.body: Client files, code and the shopping list run on one Companion Core, under the two glazed gables.

closing.body: Your client files and parts lists can sit on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: The Library Lounge has no desk and no bookshelf in the spec: Ruth works from the sofa and the trunk coffee table. Her anchors are the couch, the room and the Core (on a credenza). The print merge is at the Dining trestle table.
No TV and no kitchen island in this house (homeFlags). The media beat is Navidrome from a phone at the couch; kitchen beats say the counter, the range and the fridge.
Noam's beats sit on the Upper Landing standing desk; lupin uses the loft sofa (couch nth 1), notebook the landing bookshelf (nth 1). ruth-flow is Noam's beat in Ruth's chapter, anchored on the room.
Dahlia is Hermes (first Hermes beat is ftue-hello, both Hermes beats carry the chat-service note). Lupin is OpenClaw and carries the websites note. No cloud key, no Companion Memory in this file.
The rover is Noam's weekend hobby, not work code. The garden role resolves to the two daisy beds on the front lawn; the deck beat uses patio-seat nth 1, the Deck Dining outdoor table.
Open WebUI sits in with on landing-notebook, never as a beat app: its replaces chip would trip cap-parity. The Pi-hole beat says devices that use it for DNS, and one household instance.
